newsitem.title: USA: More US fund managers bullish on stocks - Oct survey.
newsitem.headline: More US fund managers bullish on stocks - Oct survey.

text.p: U.S. mutual fund managers no longer intend to reduce their exposure to U.S. stocks, according to a Merrill Lynch /Gallup survey.

Managers were more bullish in October than in September about the three-month outlook for U.S. equities, according to the survey. In October about 40 percent of managers were bullish, and 18 percent bearish, versus 25 percent were bullish and 18 percent were bearish in September. The balance were neutral.
The most popular sector among managers is financial services, followed by technology and energy.
Fewer managers were bullish about the U.S. economy. About 22 percent thought the U.S. economy would show improvement in terms of growth in the coming year, and 38 percent thought it would worsen.
In September, 34 percent thought the economy would improve, and 32 percent thought it would deteriorate.
Managers turned more bullish on equities in the United Kingdom, but more bearish on Japanese stocks.
